findings.fix: Delete this bullet. The `tools: Grep, Glob, Read, LS` allowlist already blocks edits, so the line restates what the harness enforces.

findings.evidence: 1. Cover the requested pattern types (feature, structural, integration, testing) as relevant, and always open the callers and the tests that exercise each candidate.
findings.fix: Give a search order the model would not come up with on its own, for example: grep the defining symbol or behavior term first, follow re-exports to the definition, then grep the definition's name for callers and test files. Also say which pattern types apply by default when the caller names none.

findings.evidence: - Grep respects `.gitignore`, so generated or vendored code may be hidden: state any scope you did not search.
findings.fix: Add the action to take: when the pattern probably lives in ignored paths (for example `vendor/`, `dist/` or generated clients), Read or Glob those directories directly by path before you report the scope as unsearched.

findings.evidence: Keep snippets to about 40 lines; when the smallest complete section is longer, quote its signature plus the essential lines and cite the full range, or exceed 40 with a one-line reason
findings.fix: Set one default and one escape hatch, for example: by default, quote the signature plus the essential lines and cite the full range. Exceed 40 lines only when the caller asks for the complete section.

findings.evidence: Copies of one upstream source are one pattern, not a repository-wide convention: label the provenance and cite the maintained source.
findings.fix: Resolve the case where the maintained source is outside the repository or in a scope you did not search: cite the most-used in-repo copy with `file:line`, name the upstream source from its header, license or package manifest, and mark it 'upstream, not in searched scope'.
